scope: Exact-subject photo candidates for destination IDs 60 and 62; research only, no active catalog changes
result: Exact subjects were found and inspected, but no public reuse license was established for these photographs.

candidates.author: Maqsad Khabibullayev / UzA
candidates.authorEvidence: Article photo credit and embedded watermark 'Maqsad Habibullayev'
candidates.rightsEvidence: UzA's own subdomain footer requires prior written editorial permission to copy, distribute or otherwise use O'zA materials. This is not a granted photo license.
candidates.picturedSubject: Chimboy jeweler Odilboy/Adil Tojimuratov working at his bench
candidates.subjectEvidence: UzA article explicitly identifies the jeweler and his father Dariboy; title and photo relate to that named maker.
candidates.visualInspection: Jeweler in a black shirt uses a flame and hand tools at a red workbench. UzA and photographer watermark is visible; this is an exact working portrait, not generic jewelry.
candidates.changes: None; original JPEG download retained; watermark preserved.

relatedButNotExactPhoto.rightsEvidence: Publisher footer states All Rights Reserved.
relatedButNotExactPhoto.visualInspection: Visitors in a room filled with paintings, sculptures and ceramics. The article covers both Adil's workshop and his father Daribay's home museum; this main image visibly emphasizes the family art museum, not jewelry making.
relatedButNotExactPhoto.decision: Do not substitute this family-museum view for a verified photograph of Adil's jewelry workshop.

supportingDocuments.evidence: Printed page 79 describes Azatbay Otarbaev's workshop and UNESCO-supported reconstruction in 2012.
supportingDocuments.notes: No photograph with an explicit reuse license was established. UNESCO support or archive hosting alone does not grant a blanket license for third-party photographs.

otherSourcesReviewed.result: License covers National PR-Centre digital content on uzbekistan.travel and its subdomains. No exact workshop photograph was located there; do not apply this license to regional tourism or news publishers.
Identifies Adil Tajimuratov and his father's workshop/home museum, but no applicable image reuse permission was established. This is a different domain from uzbekistan.travel.

Exact Adil jewelry section and photographer Azamat Matkarimov identified. Publisher terms require prior written permission, retain watermarks, and restrict modifications/commercial image reuse. Not publication-ready.
Article confirms 5 May 2012 workshop opening, but its linked image returns 404 and reuse terms require written permission.
Spring 2020 magazine credits jeweler Adil Tajimuratov and photographer Arslan Kannazarov for costume/jewelry pages. No photo reuse license was established.

searchNotes: Searched English, Russian and Uzbek name variants including Otarbayev/Otarbaev, Azatbay, Tajimuratov/Tojimuratov and Odilboy.
Targeted Wikimedia Commons, Flickr and National tourism searches did not confirm an exact-subject photograph with a reusable license.
All six downloaded JPEG candidates were visually inspected. No downloaded photograph was added to the active destination catalog or marked reuse-verified.
A full ICHCAP survey-report download stalled and was cancelled; its empty partial file was removed. The smaller safeguarding source PDF was downloaded successfully.
